items.name: Hermitian spaces and lattices over an unramified quadratic extension
items.statement: F/F_0 unramified quadratic, residue field k = F_q. Hermitian spaces are classified by dimension and disc(V) = (−1)^{n(n−1)/2} det(V) ∈ F_0^×/Nm F^× [Jac62, Thm. 3.1]; V is split if disc = 1 and nonsplit otherwise. For an integral O_F-lattice L (L ⊆ L^∨): fundamental invariants 0 ≤ a_1 ≤ ⋯ ≤ a_n with L^∨/L ≅ ⊕ O_F/ϖ^{a_i}, val(L) = Σ a_i, type t(L) = #{a_i > 0}; vertex (minuscule) lattices L ⊆ L^∨ ⊆ ϖ^{−1}L, Vert^t the vertex lattices of type t; self-dual = type 0, almost self-dual = type 1. If V is split, val(L) is even and V contains a self-dual lattice; if nonsplit, val(L) is odd and V contains an almost self-dual lattice.
items.note: GN.2 plans local classification with integral lattices and hermitian variants.

items.name: Lemma 1.9.1 (isotropic subspaces of a unitary space over F_q)
items.statement: For a nondegenerate F_{q²}/F_q-hermitian space of dimension m, the number of totally isotropic subspaces of dimension b is S_{m,b} = Π_{i=m−2b+1}^{m} (1 − (−q)^i) / Π_{i=1}^{b} (1 − q^{2i}) (orbit–stabilizer for U_m(k) and the Siegel-type parabolic P_b).
items.note: Checked against known counts: S_{2,1} = q + 1, S_{3,1} = q³ + 1, S_{4,2} = (q + 1)(q³ + 1), S_{5,2} = (q³ + 1)(q⁵ + 1). Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Local densities of hermitian lattices
items.statement: For hermitian O_F-lattices L (rank n) and M (rank m), Rep_{M,L}(R) = Herm(L ⊗ R, M ⊗ R) and Den(M, L) = lim_N #Rep_{M,L}(O_{F_0}/ϖ^N)/q^{N·dim(Rep_{M,L})_{F_0}}. If (Rep_{M,L})_{F_0} ≠ ∅ then n ≤ m and dim = dim U_m − dim U_{m−n} = n(2m − n) (3.1.0.2).
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: The normalized local Siegel series Den(X, L) and its central derivative
items.statement: Den(⟨1⟩^{n+k}, L) is a polynomial in (−q)^{−k} with Q-coefficients [Hir98, Thm. II], and Den(⟨1⟩^{n+k}, ⟨1⟩^n) = Π_{i=1}^{n}(1 − (−q)^{−i}X)|_{X=(−q)^{−k}} (3.2.0.1). Den(X, L) ∈ Z[X] is the polynomial with Den((−q)^{−k}, L) = Den(⟨1⟩^{n+k}, L)/Den(⟨1⟩^{n+k}, ⟨1⟩^n). Den(L) := Den(1, L), and when val(L) is odd, ∂Den(L) := −(d/dX)|_{X=1} Den(X, L). Both depend only on the fundamental invariants.
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Functional equation of the local Siegel series
items.statement: Den(X, L) = (−X)^{val(L)} · Den(1/X, L) (3.2.0.2) [Hir12, Thm. 5.3]; in particular Den(L) = 0 when val(L) is odd.
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Cancellation law for local densities
items.statement: For a self-dual M of rank m and an integral L^♭ of rank n: Den(⟨1⟩^{n+m+k}, L^♭ ⊕ M) = Den(⟨1⟩^{n+k}, L^♭), hence Den(X, L^♭ ⊕ M) = Den(X, L^♭) (3.2.1.1).
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Counting isometries of hermitian spaces over F_q
items.statement: If U is an F_{q²}/F_q-hermitian space of dimension n whose radical has dimension a, and V is nondegenerate of dimension m ≥ n, the number of isometries U → V is q^{n(2m−n)} Π_{i=0}^{n+a−1}(1 − (−q)^{i−m}); with m = n + k this is q^{n(2m−n)}·Den(⟨1⟩^{n+k}, ⟨1⟩^n)·m(a; (−q)^{−k}) (hermitian analogue of [Kit93, §5.6, Exercise 4]).
items.note: Checked for n = a = 1: the count is (q^m − (−1)^m)(q^{m−1} + (−1)^m), the number of nonzero isotropic vectors. Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 3.5.1 (Cho–Yamauchi formula)
items.statement: With m(a; X) = Π_{i=0}^{a−1}(1 − (−q)^iX) and m(a) = −(d/dX)|_{X=1} m(a; X) = Π_{i=1}^{a−1}(1 − (−q)^i) (m(0) = 0, m(1) = 1): Den(X, L) = Σ_{L ⊆ L′ ⊆ L′^∨} X^{2ℓ(L′/L)} m(t(L′); X), the sum over integral lattices L′ ⊇ L, ℓ = length_{O_F}. Valid also for residue characteristic 2 (F/F_0 unramified; [GY00, §9]); proved as in [CY18, Cor. 3.11].
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Example 3.5.2 (rank one)
items.statement: If rank L = 1, Den(X, L) = Σ_{i=0}^{val(L)} (−X)^i; if val(L) is odd, Den(L) = 0 and ∂Den(L) = (val(L) + 1)/2.
items.note: Printed "if val(L^♭) is odd" (sourceIssues E4). Rederived from Theorem 3.5.1. Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Corollary 3.5.3 (weighted lattice count for ∂Den)
items.statement: If val(L) is odd then every integral L′ ⊇ L has val(L′) ≡ val(L) mod 2 and t(L′) > 0, and ∂Den(L) = Σ_{L ⊆ L′ ⊆ L′^∨} m(t(L′)).
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Corollary 3.6.1 (special values)
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Corollary 3.6.2 (value at −q)
items.note: Rederived from Theorem 3.5.1 and the functional equation. Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 3.7.1 (induction formula)
items.statement: Let L^♭ have rank n − 1 and fundamental invariants (a_1, …, a_{n−1}), and x ⊥ L^♭ with val(x) > a_{n−1}. With L = L^♭ + ⟨x⟩ and L′ = L^♭ + ⟨ϖ^{−1}x⟩: Den(X, L) = X² Den(X, L′) + (1 − X) Den(−qX, L^♭) ([Ter13a, Thm. 5.1]; orthogonal case [Kat99, Thm. 2.6(1)]).
items.note: Checked in rank one. Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Lattice notation for L^♭: (L^♭)^{∨,∘}, e_max and M(L^♭)
items.statement: For integral L^♭ of rank n − 1 with L^♭_F nondegenerate: (L^♭)^{∨,∘} = {x ∈ (L^♭)^∨ : (x, x) ∈ O_F}; e_max(L^♭) = a_{n−1}; M(L^♭) = L^♭ ⊕ ⟨u⟩ with u ⊥ L^♭ of valuation a_{n−1} or a_{n−1} + 1 (⟨u⟩ = {x ⊥ L^♭ : val(x) ≥ a_{n−1}}), with invariants (a_1, …, a_{n−1}, a_{n−1}) or (…, a_{n−1} + 1). If L^♭ ⊆ L′^♭ then e_max(L′^♭) ≤ e_max(L^♭) and M(L^♭) ⊆ M(L′^♭) (7.1.0.4).
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 7.2.1 and Lemma 7.2.2 (lattices with prescribed intersection)
items.statement: For an O_F-lattice L′^♭ ⊂ L^♭_F: u ↦ L′^♭ + ⟨u⟩ is a bijection [(V/L′^♭) \ (L′^♭_F/L′^♭)]/O_F^× → {rank-n lattices L′ with L′ ∩ L^♭_F = L′^♭}. For V = L^♭_F ⊕ ⟨x⟩_F and a lattice L′, the projections induce isomorphisms π^♭(L′)/L′^♭ ≅ L′/(L′^♭ ⊕ L′_x) ≅ π_x(L′)/L′_x of cyclic O_F-modules; if x ⊥ L^♭, vol(L′) = vol(L′^♭)·vol(π_⊥(L′)) (7.2.2.1).
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 8.2.2 (when adding x does not lower the first invariants)
items.statement: For x ∈ V \ L^♭_F with L^♭ + ⟨x⟩ of fundamental invariants (a′_1, …, a′_n): a′_1 + ⋯ + a′_{n−1} ≥ a_1 + ⋯ + a_{n−1} if and only if x ∈ M(L^♭). (Via the minimal valuation of (n − 1)-minors of the fundamental matrix.)
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 9.1.1 (cancellation for an almost self-dual target)
items.statement: For k ≥ 0, M = ⟨1⟩^{n−1+k} ⊕ ⟨ϖ⟩, M̃ = ⟨1⟩^{n+1+k}, L^♯ = L ⊕ ℓ with ℓ = ⟨u_0⟩, (u_0, u_0) = ϖ: Den(M, L) = Den(M̃, L^♯)/Den(M̃, ℓ). (For i ≥ 2 the orthogonal complement in M̃_i of the image of ℓ_i is isomorphic to M_i, so restriction to ℓ_i has fibres of constant size.)
items.note: Dimension count checked. Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 9.1.2 (local density for an almost self-dual lattice)
items.note: The algebra with (3.2.0.1) and Den(X, ℓ) = 1 − X was checked. Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Definition 9.1.4 (Siegel series relative to Λ)
items.statement: Den_Λ(X, L) ∈ Z[X] with Den_Λ((−q)^{−k}, L) = Den(Λ ⊕ ⟨1⟩^k, L)/Den(⟨1⟩^{n−1} ⊕ ⟨1⟩^k, ⟨1⟩^{n−1}); by Theorem 9.1.2 Den_Λ(X, L) = Den(X, L^♯) (9.1.4.2). If val(L) is even, Den_Λ(1, L) = 0 and ∂Den_Λ(L) := −(d/dX)|_{X=1} Den_Λ(X, L).
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Example 9.1.3 (rank two: Sankaran and Terstiege)
items.statement: For L = ⟨ϖ^a⟩ ⊕ ⟨ϖ^b⟩, a ≤ b, a + b even, ε = b mod 2: the left side of Theorem 9.1.2 equals Sankaran's expression (9.1.3.1) [San17, Prop. 3.1], and Den(X, L^♯) equals Terstiege's (9.1.3.2) [Ter13a, proof of Thm. 5.2]; the two agree (same values at (0, 0), (1, 1), same a-dependent part, same difference equation in b).
items.note: Checked symbolically (sympy): (9.1.3.1) = (9.1.3.2) for all 0 ≤ a ≤ b ≤ 7 (either parity), and (9.1.3.2) satisfies the functional equation with val = a + b + 1. Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Fourier transform on a hermitian space
items.statement: For ψ : F_0 → C^× unramified (conductor O_{F_0}) and f ∈ L¹(V): f̂(x) = ∫_V f(y) ψ(tr_{F/F_0}(x, y)) dy with the self-dual Haar measure (so f̂̂(x) = f(−x)). For an O_F-lattice L of rank n (F/F_0 unramified): 1̂_L = vol(L)1_{L^∨} and vol(L) = [L^∨ : L]^{−1/2} = q^{−val(L)}.
items.note: Routed to MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.2/MP.3 as a source.

items.name: The Weil representation of SL_2(F) and the Weil constant
items.statement: For an even-dimensional quadratic space (V, ( , )) over a local field F of characteristic ≠ 2 (residue characteristic 2 allowed): ω(diag(a, a^{−1}))φ(x) = χ_V(a)|a|^{d/2}φ(ax), ω(n(b))φ(x) = ψ(½b(x, x))φ(x), ω(w)φ = γ_V φ̂ (8.1.2.1), with χ_V the quadratic character of V and γ_V the Weil constant. For the nonsplit hermitian V_n (viewed via tr_{F/F_0}), γ_V = −1.
items.note: Routed to MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.2/MP.3 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 8.1.2 and Corollary 8.1.4 (uncertainty principle, quadratic case)
items.statement: With V^∘ = {val((x, x)/2) ≥ 0} and V^{∘∘} = {val((x, x)/2) > 0}: if φ ∈ C_c^∞(V) has supp φ ⊆ V^{∘∘} and supp φ̂ ⊆ V^∘ then φ = 0; in particular if supp φ ⊆ V^{∘∘} and φ̂ is a multiple of φ then φ = 0. Proof: reduce to even dimension by doubling; φ is fixed by N(ϖ^{−1}O_F) and N^−(O_F), which generate SL_2(F), so φ is supported on the null cone and vanishes.
items.note: The generation claim was checked on the Bruhat–Tits tree: SL_2(O_F) together with any element outside it generates SL_2(F). Routed to MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.2/MP.3 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 8.1.6 (uncertainty principle, hermitian case)
items.statement: For a hermitian space over a possibly ramified quadratic F/F_0 (char F_0 ≠ 2), with V^∘ = {val(x) ≥ 0}, V^{∘∘} = {val(x) > 0}: if supp φ ⊆ V^{∘∘} and supp φ̂ ⊆ V^∘ then φ = 0 (apply Proposition 8.1.2 to (x, y)_{F_0} = tr_{F/F_0}(x, y), for which (x, x)_{F_0}/2 = (x, x)).
items.note: Routed to MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.2/MP.3 as a source.

items.name: The Weil representation of U(n, n) × U(𝕍) and Siegel–Weil sections
items.statement: For χ with χ|_{A_{F_0}^×} = η^n and ψ : A_{F_0}/F_0 → C^×, ω = ω_{χ,ψ} on S(𝕍^n): ω(m(a))ϕ(x) = χ(det a)|det a|_F^{n/2}ϕ(x·a), ω(n(b))ϕ(x) = ψ(tr bT(x))ϕ(x), ω(w_n)ϕ = γ_𝕍^n ϕ̂, ω(h)ϕ(x) = ϕ(h^{−1}x). Φ_ϕ(g) = ω(g)ϕ(0) ∈ I_n(0, χ), with its standard section Φ_ϕ(−, s) ∈ I_n(s, χ) (the standard Siegel–Weil section).
items.note: Routed to MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.2/MP.3 as a source.

items.name: Tate's theorem for p-divisible groups
items.statement: For p-divisible groups G, H over O_K (K/Q_p finite, or over O_K for K finite over F̆): Hom(G, H) ≅ Hom_{Γ_K}(T_pG, T_pH) [Tat67, Thm. 4, Cor. 1].
items.note: Routed to FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1 as a source.

items.name: Breuil's classification of p-divisible groups over O_K
items.statement: Over O_K totally ramified of degree e over W with Eisenstein polynomial E(u), p-divisible groups are classified by Breuil modules M(G) = D(G)(S) over Breuil's ring S (p-adic completion of the divided-power envelope of W[u] at (E(u))), with Fil¹M(G) and φ_M; M(G)/uM(G) is the Dieudonné module of G_k̄ and M(G) ⊗_S O_K = D(G)(O_K) [Bre00; Kis06, App.; BC, §12.2].
items.note: R07.4 plans the classification of finite flat and p-divisible groups by (Breuil–)Kisin modules. The O_{F_0}-relative version is a separate item.

items.name: Dieudonné–Manin classification
items.statement: Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p, p-divisible groups are classified up to isogeny by their slopes; used to show that a p-divisible O_{F_0}-module isogenous to Ē^{n−1} × X′ is supersingular.
items.note: R07.2 plans Dieudonné theory with slopes and the ordinary/supersingular cases.

items.name: The unitary Rapoport–Zink space N_n
items.statement: For p > 2 and F/F_0 unramified: a hermitian O_F-module of signature (1, n − 1) over a Spf O_F̆-scheme S is (X, ι, λ) with X a formal p-divisible O_{F_0}-module of relative height 2n and dimension n, ι : O_F → End(X) with Kottwitz condition charpoly(ι(a) | Lie X) = (T − a)(T − σ(a))^{n−1}, and λ a principal polarization with Rosati involution σ. N_n represents (X, ι, λ, ρ) with ρ a height-0 O_F-linear quasi-isogeny to the unique framing object (𝕏, ι_𝕏, λ_𝕏) over k̄ compatible with λ. N_n is formally locally of finite type and formally smooth of relative dimension n − 1 over Spf O_F̆ [RZ96; Mih16, Prop. 1.3].
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (parent PELModuli).

items.name: The framing object 𝔼 and its canonical lifting
items.statement: 𝔼 is the formal O_{F_0}-module of height 2 and dimension 1 over k̄, D = End°(𝔼) the quaternion division algebra, ι_𝔼 : F → D, λ_𝔼 principal; (𝔼, ι_𝔼, λ_𝔼) has signature (1, 0), N_1 ≅ Spf O_F̆, and the canonical lifting ℰ of 𝔼 over Spf O_F̆ with its framing and polarization. 𝔼̄ and ℰ̄ carry the conjugate O_F-action ι ∘ σ.
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (parent PELModuli).

items.name: The hermitian space 𝕍_n of special quasi-homomorphisms
items.statement: 𝕍_n = Hom°_{O_F}(𝔼̄, 𝕏) with (x, y) = λ_𝔼^{−1} ∘ y^∨ ∘ λ_𝕏 ∘ x ∈ End°_{O_F}(𝔼̄) ≅ F; it is the unique nondegenerate nonsplit F/F_0-hermitian space of dimension n, Hom_{O_F}(𝔼̄, 𝕏) is an integral lattice in it, and U(𝕍)(F_0) acts on N_n [KR11, Def. 3.1].
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (parent PELModuli).

items.name: Relative Dieudonné theory for strict formal O_{F_0}-modules
items.statement: For ϖ-divisible O_{F_0}-modules: the O_{F_0}-relative Dieudonné crystal and Grothendieck–Messing theory (used to show a point of Z(L^♭)(O_K) has a unique lift to O_K[ε]), and relative Breuil modules over the ϖ-adic completion of the O_{F_0}-divided-power envelope of O_F̆[u] at (E(u)) [Hen16; Fal02].
items.note: AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4 and FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.4/R07.6 plan the Z_p-versions only. Routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (parent PELModuli).

items.name: The Rapoport–Zink space N^1_n at almost self-dual level
items.statement: As N_n but with ker λ ⊆ Y[ι(ϖ)] of order q² [RSZ18, §5]; N^1_n is a formal scheme, locally formally of finite type, regular, of relative dimension n − 1 with semistable reduction over Spf O_F̆ [RSZ18, Thm. 5.1; Cho18, Thm. 1.2]. 𝕎_n = Hom°_{O_F}(𝔼, 𝕐) is a split hermitian space of dimension n.
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (parent PELModuli).

items.name: The auxiliary Rapoport–Zink space Ñ^1_n
items.statement: Fix α : 𝕐 × 𝔼 → 𝕏_{n+1} with ker α ⊆ (𝕐 × 𝔼)[ϖ] and α^*(λ_𝕏) = λ_𝕐 × ϖλ_𝔼; x_0 ∈ 𝕍_{n+1} its restriction to 𝔼 has (x_0, x_0) = ϖ and 𝕍_{n+1} = 𝕎_n ⊕ ⟨x_0⟩_F. Ñ^1_n ⊆ N^1_n × N_{n+1} is the closed formal subscheme where α lifts (uniquely) to α̃; π_1 : Ñ^1_n → N^1_n and π_2 : Ñ^1_n → N_{n+1} are the projections. On generic fibres π_1 is finite étale of degree [K : K̃] = q + 1 (Remark 10.2.1: K = Aut(Λ), K^♯ = Aut(Λ^♯), K̃ = K ∩ K^♯).
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (parent PELModuli).

items.name: The unitary Shimura datum (G̃, h_G̃)
items.statement: F CM with totally real F_0, CM type Φ with distinguished φ_0, V hermitian of dimension n ≥ 2 with signature (n − 1, 1) at φ_0 and (n, 0) elsewhere. G^Q = {g ∈ Res_{F_0/Q} GU(V) : c(g) ∈ G_m}, Z^Q the torus of a totally positive definite line, G̃ = Z^Q ×_{G_m} G^Q ≅ Z^Q × Res_{F_0/Q} U(V) (11.2.0.1), h_G̃ = (h_{Z^Q}, h_{G^Q}); reflex field E = E_r E_Φ; Sh_K has dimension n − 1 and a canonical model over E.
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (parent PELModuli).

items.name: Semi-global models at hyperspecial level (Rapoport–Smithling–Zhang)
items.statement: Under (H1)–(H4) (v_0 inert, possibly ramified over p; V_{v_0} split with K_{G,v_0} the stabilizer of a self-dual lattice; vertex-lattice stabilizers at other nonsplit v | p, arbitrary open compact at split v; arbitrary K^p_G), the groupoid of tuples (A_0, ι_0, λ_0, A, ι, λ, η̄^p, η̄^{v_0}_p) subject to (M1)–(M9) (Kottwitz, Rosati, prime-to-p level, split-place level, (A_0, ι_0, λ_0) ∈ M_0^{a,ξ}, kernel conditions on λ_v, Eisenstein and sign conditions) is represented by a Deligne–Mumford stack M_K smooth over O_{E,(ν)} with generic fibre the canonical model [RSZ17b, Thm. 4.1; RSZ19, Thm. 5.6(c); Liu18, Prop. C.20].
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (parent PELModuli).

items.name: Semi-global models at almost self-dual parahoric level
items.statement: Under (A1)–(A2) (v_0 inert and unramified over p; V_{v_0} nonsplit with K_{G,v_0} the stabilizer of an almost self-dual lattice), the same moduli problem with λ_{v_0} almost principal is represented by a Deligne–Mumford stack flat over O_{E,(ν)} [RSZ17b, Thm. 4.7], with semistable reduction when ν is unramified over p [Cho18, Prop. 1.4].
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (parent PELModuli).

items.name: Semi-global models at split places, with and without Drinfeld level
items.statement: (S) v_0 split: adding (MS) (A[w_0^∞] Lubin–Tate of type r|_{w_0}) gives M_K smooth over O_{E,(ν)} [RSZ17b, Thm. 4.2]. Under (D)(a) (ν matches Φ) and (D)(b) (E_ν/E_{r|v_0} unramified), adding a Drinfeld level structure η_{w_0} : ϖ^{−m}Λ_{w_0}/Λ_{w_0} → Hom(A_0[w_0^m], A[w_0^m]) gives a regular Deligne–Mumford stack M_{K_m}, flat over O_{E,(ν)} and finite flat over M_K [RSZ17b, Thm. 4.5, with (D)(b) added for regularity].
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (parent PELModuli).

items.name: Semi-global models at ramified places (Krämer model)
items.statement: (R) v_0 ramified in F (p ≠ 2) and unramified over p: adding the Pappas wedge condition (MR) gives a Deligne–Mumford stack flat over O_{E,(ν)} with isolated singularities [RSZ19, Thm. 5.4, Thm. 6.7]; blowing up gives the regular Krämer model [RSZ19, Def. 6.10].
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (parent PELModuli).

items.name: The model M_{K∩K^♯} and the diagram M ← M_{K∩K^♯} → M^♯
items.statement: With V^♯ = V ⊕ ⟨x_0⟩, (x_0, x_0) = u_0 of valuation 1 at v_0 and 0 at other v | p, and levels K^♯ (self-dual Λ^♯_{v_0}; Λ_v ⊕ ⟨x_0⟩ elsewhere), M_{K∩K^♯}(S) consists of a point of M, a point of M^♯ with the same (A_0, ι_0, λ_0), and an isogeny α : A × A_0 → A^♯ of degree q_{v_0} with ker α ⊆ (A × A_0)[u_0] and α^*λ^♯ = λ × u_0λ_0; it extends the Shimura-variety diagram (13.4.0.1).
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (parent PELModuli).

items.name: Global integral models at minimal and Drinfeld levels
items.statement: For Λ ⊆ V satisfying (G0)–(G4) (p = 2 only at places unramified in F; self-dual at inert split-V places, almost self-dual and unramified over p at inert nonsplit places, self-dual at split places, self-dual and unramified over p at ramified places), the moduli of (A_0, ι_0, λ_0, A, ι, λ) with (M6), (M7), (M9), (MS), (MR) is a Deligne–Mumford stack M_{K°} flat over O_E, with isolated singularities only at ramified characteristics (resolved by the Krämer model), whose base change to each O_{E,(ν)} is the semi-global model. Under (G5), M_{K_m} (normalization in Sh_{K_m}) is finite flat over M_{K°}; it is regular if every place over a (G2) place is unramified over p, and relatively representable over M_0^{a,ξ} for m large.
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (parent PELModuli).

items.name: p-adic uniformization of the supersingular locus
items.statement: For p > 2: M̂^{ss} ≅ G̃′(Q)\[N′ × G̃(A^p_f)/K^p] (13.1.0.1), where G̃′ is attached to V′ (signature (n, 0) at φ_0 and the invariant at v_0 switched), and N′ ≅ (Z^Q(Q_p)/K_{Z^Q,p}) × N_{O_{Ĕ_ν}} × Π_{v≠v_0} U(V)(F_{0,v})/K_{G,v}, with N = N_{F_{w_0}/F_{0,v_0},n} (hyperspecial case) or N^1 (almost self-dual case), and N = Ñ^1 for M_{K∩K^♯} [RZ96; Cho18, Thm. 4.3; RSZ17b, proof of Thm. 8.15; Mih16, Thm. 4.1 when v_0 is ramified over p].
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (parent PELModuli).

items.name: Complex uniformization
items.statement: Sh_K(C) = G̃(Q)\[D_{n−1} × G̃(A_f)/K] (15.1.0.1), with D_{n−1} ≅ U(n − 1, 1)/(U(n − 1) × U(1)) the negative lines in V_{φ_0}, identified with the open unit ball in C^{n−1}.
items.note: V1 plans the analytic tower Sh_K(C) = G(Q)\[X × G(A_f)/K] for general data.

items.name: Kudla–Rapoport cycles Z(L)
items.statement: For L ⊆ 𝕍, Z(L) ⊆ N represents (X, ι, λ, ρ) such that for every x ∈ L the quasi-homomorphism ρ^{−1} ∘ x ∘ ρ_𝔼̄ extends to a homomorphism ℰ̄_S → X [KR11, Def. 3.2]; Z(L) depends only on the O_F-span of L.
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Kudla–Rapoport divisors and difference divisors
items.statement: Each Z(x), x ≠ 0, is a Cartier divisor on N [KR11, Prop. 3.5]; the difference divisor D(y) = Z(y) − Z(y/ϖ) is effective and regular [Ter13b], and Z(y) = Σ_{i≥0} D(y/ϖ^i) (locally finite).
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: K-theory with supports on formal schemes
items.statement: For X locally noetherian (an increasing union of noetherian opens) and closed Y: K_0^Y(X) (finite complexes of locally free sheaves acyclic off Y) with the codimension filtration F^iK_0^Y(X) and graded pieces Gr^i [Zha19, (B.1)–(B.2)]; K′_0; for regular X, K_0^Y(X) ≅ K′_0(Y); derived intersections Z_1 ∩^L ⋯ ∩^L Z_m = O_{Z_1} ⊗^L ⋯ ⊗^L O_{Z_m}; χ(X, F) = Σ (−1)^{i+j} length H^i(X, H^j(F)); if F_i ∈ F^{r_i} with Σ r_i ≥ dim X then χ(X, ⊗^L F_i) depends only on the images in Gr^{r_i} [Zha19, (B.3)]; pullback and proper pushforward.
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Definitions 2.4.1–2.4.2 (derived cycles and the intersection number Int(L))
items.statement: For L ⊆ 𝕍 of rank r with basis x_1, …, x_r: ^ℒZ(L) is the image of O_{Z(x_1)} ⊗^L ⋯ ⊗^L O_{Z(x_r)} ∈ F^rK_0^{Z(L)}(N) in Gr^r; for r = n, Int(L) := χ(N, ^ℒZ(L)) (2.4.2.1) (= χ(N, O_{Z(x_1)} ⊗^L ⋯ ⊗^L O_{Z(x_n)}), (1.2.0.1)).
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Example 2.4.3 (rank one)
items.statement: If rank L = 1 then Int(L) = (val(L) + 1)/2, by the theory of canonical liftings [Gro86].
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Generalized Deligne–Lusztig varieties Y_V
items.statement: For the (unique) k_F/k-hermitian space V of odd dimension 2d + 1, Y_V ⊆ Gr_{d+1}(V) parametrizes U of dimension d + 1 with U^⊥ ⊆ U [Vol10, (2.19)]; it is smooth projective of dimension d with a stratification Y_V = ⊔_{i=0}^d X_{P_i}(w_i) into generalized Deligne–Lusztig varieties [Vol10, Thm. 2.15], the open stratum Y°_V a classical Deligne–Lusztig variety of Coxeter type, the others parabolic inductions of Coxeter-type varieties of Levi subgroups [HLZ19, Prop. 2.5.1].
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Minuscule Kudla–Rapoport cycles V(Λ)
items.statement: For a vertex lattice Λ ⊆ 𝕍, V_Λ = Λ^∨/Λ is a nondegenerate k_F-hermitian space of odd dimension t(Λ), and Z(Λ)_red ≅ Y_{V_Λ, k̄}; Z(Λ) is already reduced [LZ17, Thm. B], so V(Λ) := Z(Λ) = Z(Λ)_red has dimension (t(Λ) − 1)/2.
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: The Bruhat–Tits stratification of N_red (Vollaard–Wedhorn)
items.statement: N_red = ⋃_Λ V(Λ); V(Λ) ⊆ V(Λ′) iff Λ ⊇ Λ′; V(Λ) ∩ V(Λ′) ≠ ∅ iff Λ + Λ′ is a vertex lattice, and then equals V(Λ + Λ′); N_red = ⊔ V(Λ)°, V(Λ)° ≅ Y°_{V_Λ, k̄} [VW11, Thm. B]; the irreducible components are the V(Λ) with Λ of maximal type [VW11, Cor. C]; type-1 strata are the superspecial points. For L of rank ≥ 1, Z(L)_red = ⋃_{L⊆Λ} V(Λ) (2.7.0.1) [KR11, Prop. 4.1]. For n ≥ 3 a point is super-general if it lies on no Z(u) with val(u) = 0, equivalently in V(Λ)° with t(Λ) = n; there are none for n even.
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Lemma 2.8.1 (Tor vanishing for two KR divisors)
items.statement: For linearly independent x, y ∈ 𝕍_n, Tor_i^{O_N}(O_{Z(x)}, O_{Z(y)}) = 0 for i ≥ 1, so O_{Z(x)} ⊗^L O_{Z(y)} = O_{Z(x)} ⊗ O_{Z(y)}. (Local equations have no common divisor: induction on n through Z(u) ≅ N_{n−1}; at super-general points, D(y) and the affineness of V(Λ)° [Lus76, Cor. 2.8].)
items.note: Generalizes [Ter13a, Lemma 3.1] (n = 3). Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Corollary 2.8.2 (independence of the basis)
items.statement: For L ⊆ 𝕍 of rank r ≥ 1, O_{Z(x_1)} ⊗^L ⋯ ⊗^L O_{Z(x_r)} ∈ K_0^{Z(L)}(N) is independent of the basis x_1, …, x_r (also [How18, Cor. C]); hence Int(L) depends only on L.
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Horizontal and vertical parts (Definition 2.9.1, Lemma 2.9.2)
items.statement: Z over Spf O_F̆ is vertical if ϖ is locally nilpotent and horizontal if flat; Z_H is cut out by the torsion ideal O_{Z,tor}, and for noetherian Z, Z_V by ϖ^N O_Z (N ≫ 0), with Z = Z_H ∪ Z_V. For L of rank r ≥ n − 1, Z(L) is noetherian (finitely many vertex lattices contain L).
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Lemma 2.10.1 (finiteness of Int)
items.statement: For L ⊆ 𝕍 of rank n, Z(L) is a proper scheme over Spf O_F̆ (the horizontal part is empty, since n independent special homomorphisms would force signature (0, n)); Int(L) is finite.
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Self-dual cancellation: N_{n−r} ≅ Z(M)
items.statement: For a self-dual M ⊂ 𝕍_n of rank r, (X, ι, λ, ρ) ↦ (X × ℰ̄^r, …) gives δ_M : N_{n−r} ↪ N_n identifying N_{n−r} with Z(M) [RSZ18, Rem. 4.5] (2.11.0.1); for u ∈ 𝕍_n with projection u^♭ ≠ 0 to 𝕍_{n−r}, Z(u) meets N_{n−r} transversely and N_{n−r} ∩^L Z(u) = Z(u^♭) (2.11.0.2) [Zha19, Lemma B.2(i)].
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Lemma 2.11.1 (cancellation law for Int)
items.statement: For a self-dual M ⊂ 𝕍_n of rank r and integral L^♭ ⊆ 𝕍_{n−r}: Int(L^♭ ⊕ M) = Int(L^♭).
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Local densities as Whittaker functions
items.statement: For Λ = ⟨1⟩^n, ϕ_0 = 1_{Λ^n} and T the fundamental matrix of a basis of L: W_T(1, k, ϕ_0) = Den(⟨1⟩^{n+2k}, L) for integers k ≥ 0 [KR14, Prop. 10.1]; hence W_T(1, 0, ϕ_0) = Den(L)·Π_{i=1}^{n}(1 − (−q)^{−i}) (3.3.0.1) and W′_T(1, 0, ϕ_0) = ∂Den(L)·Π_{i=1}^{n}(1 − (−q)^{−i})·log q² (3.3.0.2). For Λ = ⟨1⟩^{n−1} ⊕ ⟨ϖ⟩ and ϕ_1 = 1_{Λ^n}: W_T(1, k, ϕ_1) = (−q)^n Den(Λ ⊕ ⟨1⟩^{2k}, L), giving (9.2.0.1)–(9.2.0.2).
items.note: Footnote 2 corrects [KR14, Prop. 9.3]: log p should be log p². Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Quasi-canonical lifting cycles on N_2
items.statement: For ⟨y⟩ ⊆ 𝕍_2 of rank one, Z(y) = Σ_{i=0}^{⌊val(y)/2⌋} Z_{val(y)−2i} as Cartier divisors on N_2 [KR11, Prop. 8.1], where Z_s ≅ Spf O_{F̆,s} is the quasi-canonical lifting cycle of level s [Gro86], O_{F̆,s} the integers of the ring class field of O_{F,s} = O_{F_0} + ϖ^sO_F, of degree q^s(1 + q^{−1}) over O_F̆ for s ≥ 1; the primitive part is Z(y)° := Z_{val(y)}.
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Primitive horizontal cycles Z(M^♭)° for t(M^♭) ≤ 1
items.statement: For integral M^♭ of rank n − 1 with t(M^♭) ≤ 1, write M^♭ = M_{n−2} ⊕ ⟨y⟩ with M_{n−2} self-dual; under Z(M_{n−2}) ≅ N_2, Z(M^♭) ↔ Z(y) = Σ Z_{val(M^♭)−2i} (4.2.0.1), and Z(M^♭)° is the component isomorphic to Z_{val(M^♭)} (independent of M_{n−2}), of O_F̆-degree 1 if t(M^♭) = 0 and vol(M^♭)^{−1}(1 + q^{−1}) if t(M^♭) = 1 (4.2.0.2).
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Theorem 4.2.1 (the horizontal part)
items.statement: For L^♭ ⊆ 𝕍_n of rank n − 1: Z(L^♭)_H = ⋃_{L^♭ ⊆ M^♭ ⊆ (M^♭)^∨, t(M^♭) ≤ 1} Z(M^♭)°, the cycles on the right being distinct (Lemma 4.2.2), and O_{Z(L^♭)_H} = Σ O_{Z(M^♭)°} in Gr^{n−1}K_0^{Z(L^♭)_H}(N_n). Proof via Tate modules (Lemmas 4.4.1, 4.5.1) for O_K-points and Breuil modules with Grothendieck–Messing for uniqueness of lifts to O_K[ε].
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Lemma 4.4.1 (special homomorphisms from the Tate module)
items.statement: For z ∈ N_n(O_K) with hermitian module G over O_K, 𝕃 = Hom_{O_F}(T_pℰ̄, T_pG) is a self-dual hermitian O_F-lattice of rank n, and Hom_{O_F}(ℰ̄, G) = i_K^{−1}(𝕃) (4.4.1.1); hence z ∈ Z(M)(O_K) iff M ⊆ i_k̄(i_K^{−1}(𝕃)) (4.4.1.2).
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Lemma 4.5.1
items.statement: If 𝕃 is a self-dual hermitian O_F-lattice of rank n and W ⊂ 𝕃_F has dimension n − 1, then t(W ∩ 𝕃) ≤ 1.
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Corollary 4.6.1 (degree of the horizontal part)
items.statement: deg_{O_F̆}(Z(L^♭)_H) = vol(L^♭)^{−1}Den((−q)^{−1}, L^♭) = Den(−q, L^♭). (Remark 4.6.2: via p-adic uniformization this gives a unitary analogue of [Kud97a, Thm. 10.6].)
items.note: Checked against (3.6.1.2) and (4.2.0.2). Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Lemma 5.1.1 (support of the vertical part)
items.statement: Z(L^♭)_V is supported on N_{n,red}: O_{Z(L^♭)_V} is killed by a power of the ideal of N_{n,red}.
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Definition 5.2.1 and Corollary 5.2.2 (splitting of the derived cycle)
items.statement: Gr^{n−1}K_0^{Z(L^♭)}(N_n) = Gr^{n−1}K_0^{Z(L^♭)_H} ⊕ Gr^{n−1}K_0^{Z(L^♭)_V} (5.2.0.1), giving ^ℒZ(L^♭) = Z(L^♭)_H + ^ℒZ(L^♭)_V, with ^ℒZ(L^♭)_V canonical (independent of N) and Z(L^♭)_H represented by its structure sheaf [Zha19, Lemma B.2(ii)]; there are finitely many curves C_i ⊆ N_{n,red} and mult_{C_i} ∈ Q with ^ℒZ(L^♭)_V = Σ mult_{C_i}[O_{C_i}] in Gr^{n−1}K_0^{N_red}(N_n).
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Lusztig's results on Coxeter varieties of unitary groups
items.statement: For the Coxeter variety Y°_d of U_{2d+1}: F = Fr_{k_F} has exactly the 2d + 1 eigenvalues (−q)^m (0 ≤ m ≤ 2d) on H_c^*(Y°_d), with (−q)^m in H_c^{⌊m/2⌋+d} [Lus76, 7.3, case ²A_{2n}; 1.18]; F acts semisimply [Lus76, 6.1]; Y°_d is affine [Lus76, Cor. 2.8].
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 5.3.1, p.25; proof of Lemma 2.8.1, pp.13–14, arXiv:1908.01701v3
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Lemma 5.3.1 (no Tate classes off the closed strata)
items.statement: For d, i ≥ 0 and s ≥ 1, F^s acts semisimply on H^{2j}(Y°_d)(j), H^{2j}(X°_i)(j) and H^{2j}(Y_d − X_i)(j), with no nonzero invariants for j ≥ 1 (the eigenvalues on H^{2j}(Y°_d)(j) are (−q)^{2j}, (−q)^{2j−1} when d ≥ 2j > 0).
items.note: The eigenvalue bookkeeping through Poincaré duality was rederived. Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: The Tate conjecture for varieties over finite fields (statement)
items.statement: For X over a finite field, the Q_ℓ-span of the ℓ-adic cycle classes of codimension-i cycles is the space of Tate classes H^{2i}(X_k̄, Q_ℓ(i))^{F^s=1} [Tat65, Conj. 1; Tat94, Conj. T^i].
items.note: MC.7 plans typed statements of the Tate conjecture and a register of proven cases.

items.name: Theorem 5.3.2 (the Tate conjecture for Y_d)
items.statement: For 0 ≤ i ≤ d and s ≥ 1: (1) H^{2i}(Y_d)(i)^{F^s=1} is spanned by the cycle classes of the irreducible components of X_{d−i}; in particular the Tate conjecture holds for Y_d. (2) The generalized 1-eigenspace of F^s on H^{2i}(Y_d)(i) equals the invariants.
items.note: A proven case to register in MC.7 once built here. Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Corollary 5.3.3 (reduction to Deligne–Lusztig curves)
items.statement: There are finitely many Deligne–Lusztig curves C_i ⊆ N_{n,red} and mult_{C_i} ∈ Q with χ(N_n, ^ℒZ(L^♭)_V ∩^L Z(x)) = Σ mult_{C_i}·χ(N_n, C_i ∩^L Z(x)) for all x ∈ 𝕍_n \ L^♭_F.
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Lemmas 5.4.3–5.4.4 (the combinatorics of n = 3)
items.statement: A unit-norm e ∈ 𝕍_3 lies in a unique type-1 vertex lattice Λ_e, which contains every integral lattice containing e (Lemma 5.4.3). For Λ_0 ∈ Vert^3(L^♭) there is a unit-norm e with M = ⟨e⟩ such that Λ_0 + M = Λ_e = L^♭_{Λ_e} ⊕ M, Λ_0 = L^♭_{Λ_0} + ϖM and L^♭_{Λ_0} = L^♭_{Λ_e}, every other Λ ∈ Vert^3(L^♭ + ϖM) has L^♭_Λ = L^♭_{ϖΛ_e^∨} of colength one in L^♭_{Λ_0}, and t(L′^♭ ⊕ M) is 2 or 1 according as L′^♭ ⊆ L^♭_{ϖΛ_e^∨} or not (Lemma 5.4.4), where L^♭_Λ = L^♭_F ∩ Λ.
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Theorem 5.4.1 (the vertical cycle for n = 3; Theorem 3.4.1 for n = 2)
items.statement: (i) For L^♭ ⊂ 𝕍_3 of rank two: Z(L^♭)_V = ^ℒZ(L^♭)_V = Σ_{Λ ∈ Vert^3(L^♭)} mult_{L^♭}(Λ)·V(Λ) in Gr², with mult_{L^♭}(Λ) = #{L′^♭ : L^♭ ⊆ L′^♭ ⊆ L^♭_Λ}. (ii) Int(L^♭) = ∂Den(L^♭) for all L^♭ ⊂ 𝕍_2 (logically independent of [KR11, Thm. 1.1]). Along the way (5.4.5.5): for Λ ∈ Vert^3 and unit-norm e, χ(N_3, V(Λ) ∩^L Z(e)) = 1 if e ∈ Λ^∨ and 0 otherwise.
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Corollary 5.4.6 (intersecting a primitive horizontal cycle)
items.statement: For integral L^♭ ⊂ 𝕍_n of rank n − 1 with t(L^♭) ≤ 1 and x ∈ 𝕍_n \ L^♭_F: χ(N_n, Z(x) ∩^L Z(L^♭)°) = Σ_{L^♭+⟨x⟩ ⊆ L′ ⊆ L′^∨, L′ ∩ L^♭_F = L^♭} m(t(L′)).
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Definitions 6.1.1–6.1.2 and Theorem 6.1.3 (the horizontal identity)
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Definition 6.1.4 (the vertical part of Int)
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Lemma 6.2.1 (intersection with a Deligne–Lusztig curve)
items.statement: For Λ ∈ Vert^3, Int_{V(Λ)} := χ(N_n, V(Λ) ∩^L Z(x)) = −q²(1 + q)1_Λ + Σ_{Λ ⊂ Λ′, t(Λ′)=1} 1_{Λ′}, i.e. 1 − q² on Λ, 1 on {x ∈ Λ^∨ \ Λ : val(x) ≥ 0}, and 0 elsewhere.
items.note: The indicator identity (6.2.1.1) was checked: q³ + 1 type-1 lattices lie over Λ. Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Corollary 6.2.2
items.statement: Int_{L^♭,V} extends to a (necessarily unique) function in C_c^∞(𝕍).
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Lemma 6.3.1 and Corollary 6.3.3 (local modularity)
items.statement: For Λ ∈ Vert^3, (Int_{V(Λ)})^ = γ_𝕍·Int_{V(Λ)} with γ_𝕍 = −1; consequently (Int_{L^♭,V})^ = γ_𝕍·Int_{L^♭,V}. (Remark 6.3.2: Int_{V(Λ)} is SL_2(O_{F_0})-invariant under the Weil representation.)
items.locator: Lemma 6.3.1, Remark 6.3.2 and Corollary 6.3.3, pp.36–37, arXiv:1908.01701v3
items.note: The four-case evaluation was rederived (values q² − 1, −1, 0, 0). Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Definitions 6.4.1 and 6.4.3, Lemma 6.4.4 (K-classes on V(Λ))
items.statement: For Λ of type 2d + 1: K̄_0(V(Λ)) = K_0(V(Λ))_Q/ker(cl ∘ ch) and Ch̄^i = Ch^i_Q/ker cl^i, with ch and cl isomorphisms onto ⊕ Tate^{2i}_ℓ(V(Λ)), which pair perfectly (6.4.0.2)–(6.4.0.4). K_{V(Λ)}(x) is the image of V(Λ) ∩^L Z(x); c_{1,V(Λ)}(x) = c_1(O_N(−Z(x))|_{V(Λ)}) ∈ Ch¹_Q and c_{V(Λ)}(x) = c_{1,V(Λ)}(x)^d ∈ Ch^d_Q ≅ Q. Both are invariant under translation by Λ, hence functions on 𝕍/Λ (Lemma 6.4.4).
items.note: The printed ch(V(Λ) ∩^L Z(x)) has the wrong sign (sourceIssues E2). Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Lemma 6.4.5
items.note: The counts q^{2(d−1)} − 1 and q^{2(d−1)}(1 + q³)(q² − 1) and the resulting sum −(1 − q²)(1 + q^{2d+1}) were checked. Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Lemma 6.4.6 (the top power of c_1), corrected
items.statement: For Λ ∈ Vert^{2d+1}: c_{V(Λ)}(x) = (−1)^d c(d)·{(1 − q^{2d}) for x ∈ Λ; 1 for x ∈ Λ^∨ \ Λ with val(x) ≥ 0; 0 otherwise}, with c(1) = 1 and c(d) = Π_{i=1}^{d−1}(1 − q^{2i}).
items.note: Printed without the factor (−1)^d (sourceIssues E2). The induction was checked: (q^{2d+1} + 1)(q^{2d} − 1) isotropic vectors. Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Lemma 6.4.7, corrected
items.note: Printed without (−1)^d (E2); its proof cites Lemma 6.3.1 for Lemma 6.2.1 (E3). Both counting identities were checked symbolically for d = 2, …, 6. Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Corollary 6.4.8 and Theorem 6.4.9 (K-theoretic local modularity)
items.statement: For Λ ∈ Vert^{2d+1}: c_{V(Λ)} ∈ C_c^∞(𝕍) satisfies ĉ_{V(Λ)} = γ_𝕍 c_{V(Λ)}; and for every linear l : K̄_0(V(Λ)) → Q, l ∘ K_{V(Λ)} extends to C_c^∞(𝕍) with (l ∘ K_{V(Λ)})^ = γ_𝕍·(l ∘ K_{V(Λ)}).
items.note: Unaffected by the sign in E2 (the identities are homogeneous). The proof of Corollary 6.4.8 cites "Lemmas 6.4.8 and 6.3.1" for 6.4.7 and 6.3.1 (E3). Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Corollary 6.4.10 (higher local modularity)
items.statement: For Λ ∈ Vert^{2d+1}, Int_{V(Λ)} extends to C_c^∞(𝕍) and (Int_{V(Λ)})^ = γ_𝕍·Int_{V(Λ)} (χ factors through K̄_0 by Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch). Remark 6.4.11: this reproves Corollary 6.3.3 without [Zha19, (B.3)] for formal schemes.
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch and the Chern character on a smooth projective variety
items.statement: ch : K_0(X)_Q → ⊕ Ch^i(X)_Q is a graded ring isomorphism (Gr^iK_0 ≅ Ch^i), and χ(X, F) = deg(ch(F)·Td(X)).

items.statement: cl : ⊕ Ch^i(X)_Q → ⊕ H^{2i}(X, Q_ℓ)(i) intertwines intersection and cup products (6.4.0.1).

items.name: Definitions 7.3.1–7.3.3 (analytic functions on 𝕍 \ L^♭_F)
items.statement: ∂Den_{L^♭}(x) := ∂Den(L^♭ + ⟨x⟩) = Σ_{L^♭ ⊆ L′ ⊆ L′^∨} m(t(L′))1_{L′}(x) (7.3.1.1); ∂Den_{L^♭,V} := ∂Den_{L^♭} − ∂Den_{L^♭,H}; L¹_c(𝕍) and logarithmic singularity along a nondegenerate hyperplane W (f(u) = C_0 log|(u_⊥, u_⊥)| + C_1 near each point).

items.name: Proposition 7.3.4 (regularity of the analytic side)
items.statement: (a) ∂Den_{L^♭,H} and ∂Den_{L^♭} lie in L¹_c(𝕍) with logarithmic singularity along L^♭_F. (b) ∂Den_{L^♭,V} extends to a (unique) element of C_c^∞(𝕍).
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Lemma 7.3.5 (differences along the normal line)
items.note: The first part was rederived from Proposition 3.7.1, and the three-case sums (7.3.5.4)–(7.3.5.5) were checked. Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Lemma 7.3.6 and Corollary 7.3.7 (Fourier transforms of the analytic side)
items.statement: The auxiliary Σ_{L^♭ ⊆ L′ ⊆ L′^∨} 1_{L′} lies in L¹_c(𝕍) with logarithmic singularity along L^♭_F; and, by dominated convergence, (∂Den_{L^♭,H})^(x) = Σ_{t(L′^♭) ≤ 1} vol(L′)m(t(L′))1_{L′^∨}(x) and (∂Den_{L^♭})^(x) = Σ vol(L′)m(t(L′))1_{L′^∨}(x), pointwise absolutely convergent.

items.name: Theorem 8.2.1 (the vertical identity)
items.statement: For L^♭ ⊂ 𝕍 of rank n − 1 with L^♭_F nondegenerate: Int_{L^♭,V} = ∂Den_{L^♭,V} in C_c^∞(𝕍). Proof by induction on val(L^♭): by Lemma 8.2.2 and the induction hypothesis the difference φ is supported in M(L^♭), so φ = 1_{L^♭} ⊗ φ_⊥; Corollary 6.3.3 and Theorem 7.4.1 give φ̂(x) = 0 for x ⊥ L^♭ with val(x) < 0, and translation invariance of φ̂_⊥ under ⟨u^∨⟩ (val(u^∨) < 0) forces φ = 0.
items.note: The proof's claimed equalities of the vertical parts for L^♭ and L′^♭ do not follow; the equality of differences does (sourceIssues E1). Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Theorem 3.4.1 = Theorem 1.2.1 (local Kudla–Rapoport conjecture)
items.statement: Let F_0/Q_p be finite with p > 2, F/F_0 unramified quadratic, and L ⊆ 𝕍_n an O_F-lattice of full rank n. Then Int(L) = ∂Den(L) [KR11, Conj. 1.3]. Equivalently (Remark 3.4.2) Int(L) = (W′_T(1, 0, ϕ_0)/log q²)·Π_{i=1}^{n}(1 − (−q)^{−i})^{−1}.
items.locator: Theorem 1.2.1, p.4; Theorem 3.4.1 and Remark 3.4.2, p.17; proof §8.2, p.58, arXiv:1908.01701v3
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Special divisors on N^1_n and Int′(L)
items.statement: For 0 ≠ x ∈ 𝕎_n, Y(x) (resp. Y′(x)) is the locus where x (resp. λ_𝕐 ∘ x) extends to ℰ̄_S → Y (resp. Y^∨); both are Cartier [Cho18, Prop. 5.9], and Y(x) ≅ N^1_{n−1} if val(x) = 0, Y′(x) ≅ N_{n−1} if val(x) = −1 (10.1.0.1) [Cho18, Prop. 5.10]. For L ⊂ 𝕎_n of rank n with basis x_i: Int′(L) := χ(N^1_n, O_{Y(x_1)} ⊗^L ⋯ ⊗^L O_{Y(x_n)}) (10.1.1.1).
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: The pulled-back divisors Z^♭(x) and the variant Int(L)
items.statement: π_2 : Ñ^1_n → N_{n+1} lands in Z(x_0), an isomorphism on generic fibres (Remark 10.2.1; Z(x_0) is regular [Ter13b]). For x ∈ 𝕎_n, Z^♭(x) := Z(x_0) ∩ Z(x) on Z(x_0) (Remark 10.2.2: an integral model of the pullback of Y(x)_η). Int(L; x_1, …, x_n) := (q + 1)^{−1} χ(Z(x_0), Z^♭(x_1) ∩^L ⋯ ∩^L Z^♭(x_n)) (10.2.3.1).
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Theorem 10.3.1 (the almost self-dual Int = ∂Den)
items.statement: For L ⊆ 𝕎_n of full rank n and any basis: Int(L; x_1, …, x_n) = (q + 1)^{−1}∂Den_Λ(L); so Int(L) is independent of the basis. (Int = Int(L^♯)/(q + 1) by Lemma 2.8.1, then Theorem 3.4.1 and (9.1.4.2).) Remark 10.3.2: Int(L) = (W′_T(1, 0, ϕ_1)/log q²)·((−q)^n − 1)/(q + 1)·Π_{i=1}^{n}(1 − (−q)^{−i})^{−1}.
items.note: Printed "L ⊆ V" for L ⊆ 𝕎_n (E4). Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Conjecture 10.4.1 (Kudla–Rapoport), assumed
items.statement: (i) π_1 is finite flat of degree q + 1, étale away from N^{1,ss}_n = ⊔_{Λ ∈ Vert^0(𝕎_n)} P_Λ (P_Λ ≅ P^{n−1} from the Bruhat–Tits stratification of N^1_n [Cho18, Rem. 2.15]) and totally ramified along it. (ii) π_2 is the blow-up of Z(x_0) along the zero-dimensional Z(x_0)^{ss} (the superspecial points V(Λ ⊕ ⟨x_0⟩), Λ ∈ Vert^0(𝕎_n)). (iii) π_1^{−1}(N^{1,ss}_n) is exactly the exceptional divisor.
items.note: Stated as observed by Kudla and Rapoport in an unpublished manuscript; the paper says [KRSZ19] (in preparation) will prove it, and assumes it from §10.4 on. No such paper was found on arXiv (searched 2026-09-22). Theorems 10.4.3 and 10.5.1 are conditional on it. Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Lemma 10.4.2
items.statement: For 0 ≠ x ∈ 𝕎_n, π_1^{−1}(Y(x)) and π_2^{−1}(Z^♭(x)) are Cartier divisors on Ñ^1_n, and π_1^*(Y(x)) = π_1^{−1}(Y(x)), π_2^*(Z^♭(x)) = π_2^{−1}(Z^♭(x)) in the relevant K-groups.
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Theorem 10.4.3 (comparison of the two divisors; conditional)
items.statement: Assuming Conjecture 10.4.1: for 0 ≠ x ∈ 𝕎_n, π_1^{−1}(Y(x)) = π_2^{−1}(Z^♭(x)) − Exp(x) as Cartier divisors on Ñ^1_n, where Exp(x) = Σ_{Λ ∈ Vert(x)} P_Λ and Vert(x) = {Λ ⊂ 𝕎_n : Λ^∨ = Λ, x ∈ Λ}.
items.note: The n = 1 step prints "Y(x) is non-empty unless val(x) ≥ 2" for "empty unless" (E4). Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Theorem 10.5.1 (Int′ in the almost self-dual case; conditional)
items.statement: Assuming Conjecture 10.4.1: for L ⊆ 𝕎_n of full rank, Int′(L) = (q + 1)^{−1}(∂Den_Λ(L) − Den(L)); in particular Int′(L) is independent of the basis. (Remark 10.5.2: n = 2 is [San17]; Example 10.5.3: for n = 1, Int′ = val(x)/2 and ∂Den_Λ = 1 + (q + 1)val(x)/2 for val(x) ≥ 0; Remark 10.5.4 gives the Whittaker form.)
items.locator: Theorem 10.5.1, Remark 10.5.2, Example 10.5.3 and Remark 10.5.4, pp.70–72, arXiv:1908.01701v3
items.note: The n = 1 case was rederived from Corollary 3.5.3. Printed "L ⊆ V" for L ⊆ 𝕎_n (E4). Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Siegel Eisenstein series on U(n, n) and their Fourier coefficients
items.statement: W the split skew-hermitian space of dimension 2n, G_n = U(W), Siegel parabolic P_n = M_nN_n; I_n(s, χ) = Ind(χ·|·|_F^{s+n/2}); for a standard section Φ, E(g, s, Φ) = Σ_{P_n(F_0)\G_n(F_0)} Φ(γg, s), convergent for Re(s) ≫ 0 with meromorphic continuation. With ψ unramified outside Spl(F/F_0) (footnote 4, via class field theory and Hecke's theorem that the different class is a square), E = Σ_T E_T, and for nonsingular T and factorizable Φ, E_T = Π_v W_{T,v}, whence E′_T = Σ_v E′_{T,v} (12.2.0.1)–(12.2.0.2).
items.note: AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.1–AS.2 plan Eisenstein series induced from cuspidal data; the degenerate Siegel series needs its own development. Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Incoherent Eisenstein series and the Diff set
items.statement: For an incoherent A_F/A_{F_0}-hermitian space 𝕍, E(g, 0, ϕ) = 0 [KR14, §9]; for nonsingular T, ∂Eis_T ≠ 0 only if Diff(T, 𝕍) = {v} is a singleton (necessarily nonsplit), and then ∂Eis_T = ∂Eis_{T,v} (12.3.0.1) [KR14, Lemma 9.1]; if ϕ is nonsingular at two finite places, ∂Eis_T = 0 for every singular T (12.3.0.2) [Liu11b, Prop. 2.1].
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: The classical incoherent Eisenstein series on H_n
items.statement: For the incoherent 𝕍 nearby V (totally positive definite, 𝕍_v ≅ V_v at finite v) and ϕ = ϕ_K ⊗ ϕ_∞ with Gaussian ϕ_∞: E(z, s, ϕ) = χ_∞(det a)^{−1}det(y)^{−n/2}E(g_z, s, ϕ) on H_n = {x + iy : y > 0}; ∂Eis(z, ϕ_K) = Σ_T ∂Eis_T(z, ϕ_K) (12.4.0.1); for T > 0, W_{T,∞}(z, 0, ϕ_∞) = c_∞q^T [Liu11a, Prop. 4.5(2)] and ∂Eis_{T,v}(z, ϕ_K) = c_∞W′_{T,v}(1, 0, ϕ_{K,v})Π_{v′≠v, v′∤∞}W_{T,v′}(1, 0, ϕ_{K,v′})q^T (12.4.0.3).
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Semi-global special homomorphisms and Kudla–Rapoport cycles Z(T, ϕ_K)
items.statement: V(A_0, A) = Hom_{O_F}(A_0, A) ⊗ Z_(p) with the O_{F,(p)}-hermitian form λ_0^{−1} ∘ y^∨ ∘ λ ∘ x, fundamental matrices T(x). For v_0-admissible ϕ_K (K-invariant, ϕ_{K,v} = 1_{(Λ_v)^m} at nonsplit v | p), first for ϕ_K = (1_{Ω_i}): Z(T, ϕ_K)(S) = points of M with x ∈ V(A_0, A)^m, T(x) = T, η^p(x) ∈ Π Ω_i^{(p)} and η_v(x) ∈ Π Ω_{i,w} at split v ≠ v_0; finite unramified over M [KR14, Prop. 2.9], extended C-linearly. At almost self-dual level, Z^♭(T, ϕ_K) on M_{K∩K^♯} via the cycle on M^♯.
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Local arithmetic intersection numbers Int_{T,v_0}(ϕ_K)
items.statement: For T ∈ Herm_n(O_{F,(p)})_{>0} with diagonal t_1, …, t_n: Int_{T,ν}(ϕ_K) = χ(Z(T, ϕ_K), O_{Z(t_1,ϕ_1)} ⊗^L ⋯ ⊗^L O_{Z(t_n,ϕ_n)})·log q_ν (self-dual case, (13.5.0.1)), and (deg π_1)^{−1}χ(Z^♭(T, ϕ_K), ⊗^L O_{Z^♭(t_i,ϕ_i)})·log q_ν (almost self-dual case, (13.5.0.2)); Int_{T,v_0} = [E : F_0]^{−1}Σ_{ν|v_0} Int_{T,ν}, extended C-linearly.
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: The Siegel–Weil formula for unitary groups (Ichino)
items.statement: The theta integral of a Schwartz function over the relevant unitary group equals the value of the associated Siegel Eisenstein series [Ich04, §6]; used to evaluate the point count away from v_0 as Π_{v≠v_0, v∤∞} W_{T,v}(1, 0, ϕ_{K,v}) up to a constant.
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Theorem 13.6.1 (the semi-global identity at an inert prime)
items.statement: In the situation of §11.2 (hyperspecial) or §11.3 (almost self-dual), with p > 2 and ϕ_K v_0-admissible: for every T ∈ Herm_n(O_{F,(p)})_{>0}, Int_{T,v_0}(ϕ_K)q^T = c_K·∂Eis_{T,v_0}(z, ϕ_K), c_K = (−1)^n/vol(K). Proof: Z(T) is supported in the supersingular locus [KR14, Lemma 2.21]; p-adic uniformization, Theorem 3.4.1 (or 10.3.1) and the Siegel–Weil formula; in the almost self-dual case also Den(Λ, Λ)/Den(⟨1⟩^{n−1}, ⟨1⟩^{n−1}) = ∂Den_Λ(L)/Int(L) = q + 1 (13.6.1.1).
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Global Kudla–Rapoport cycles and Int_T(ϕ_K)
items.statement: On M = M_{K_m}: Z(t_i, ϕ_i) the Zariski closure of the generic-fibre cycle, and Z(t_1, ϕ_1) ∩ ⋯ ∩ Z(t_m, ϕ_m) = ⊔_T Z(T, ϕ_K) over T with diagonal t_i [KR14, (11.2)]. For nonsingular T, Int_T(ϕ_K) = Σ_v Int_{T,v}(ϕ_K), nonzero only if Diff(T, V) = {v} (nonsplit), and then Int_T = Int_{T,v} (14.4.0.1).
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Theorem 14.5.1 = Theorem 1.3.1 (global Kudla–Rapoport conjecture)
items.statement: In the situation of §14.2, let ϕ_K be inert-admissible and T ∈ Herm_n(F) inert (Diff(T, V) = {v} with v inert in F and not above 2). Then Int_T(ϕ_K)q^T = c_K·∂Eis_T(z, ϕ_K), c_K = (−1)^n/vol(K).
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Corollary 14.5.2 (Kudla–Rapoport's global conjecture)
items.statement: [KR14, Conj. 11.10] holds: take F_0 = Q, K = K°, a trivial; then M_{K°} is M_V of [KR14, Prop. 2.12], ϕ_K = 1_{(Λ̂)^n} is inert-admissible, and Diff_0(T) = {p} with p > 2 makes T inert.
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Kudla's Green functions and star products
items.statement: For x ∈ V_{φ_0} nonzero and z ∈ D, R(x, z) = −(x_z, x_z), D(x) = {z ⊥ x} (nonempty iff (x, x) > 0), g(x, z) = −Ei(−2πR(x, z)) with Ei(u) = −∫_1^∞ e^{ut}/t dt; dd^c[g(x)] + δ_{D(x)} = [ω(x)], ω(x) = e^{2π(x,x)}ϕ_{KM}(x) with the Kudla–Millson form [Liu11a, Prop. 4.9; KM86]. For x with T(x) nonsingular, g(x) = [g(x_1)] ∗ ⋯ ∗ [g(x_m)] with [g(x)] ∗ [g(y)] = [g(x)] ∧ δ_{D(y)} + [ω(x)] ∧ [g(y)], and dd^c g(x) + δ_{D(x)} = [ω(x_1) ∧ ⋯ ∧ ω(x_m)].
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Archimedean intersection numbers Int_{T,φ}(y, ϕ_K)
items.statement: Z(T, ϕ_K)(C) = Σ_x Σ_g̃ ϕ_K(g̃^{−1}x)·Z(x, g̃)_K; the Green current g(y_{φ_0}, T, ϕ_K)(z, g̃) = Σ_{T(x)=T} ϕ_K(g̃^{−1}x)g(x·a, z) with y_{φ_0} = a ᵗā; Int_{T,φ}(y_φ, ϕ_K) = ½∫_{Sh^φ_K(C)} g(y_φ, T, ϕ_K) (15.3.0.1) for each φ ∈ Φ (using the conjugate Shimura variety Sh^φ_K).
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Theorem 15.3.1 (the archimedean identity)
items.statement: For K-invariant ϕ_K, nonsingular T ∈ Herm_n(F) and φ ∈ Φ: Int_{T,φ}(y, ϕ_K)q^T = c_K·∂Eis_{T,φ}(z, ϕ_K) (by [Liu11a, Prop. 4.5, Thms. 4.17, 4.20] and unfolding; alternatively [GS19, (1.19)] when V is anisotropic).
items.note: Routed to the Part II UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights).

items.name: Arithmetic degrees and the Gillet–Soulé arithmetic Chow group
items.statement: deĝ_T(y, ϕ_K) := Int_T(ϕ_K) + Σ_{φ∈Φ} Int_{T,φ}(y_φ, ϕ_K) (15.4.0.1), and deĝ(z, ϕ_K) := Σ_{det T ≠ 0} deĝ_T(y, ϕ_K)q^T. For nonzero t_i, Ẑ(y, t_i, ϕ_i) = (Z(t_i, ϕ_i), g(y, t_i, ϕ_i)) ∈ ĈH¹_C(M_K) of the regular Deligne–Mumford stack [GS90; Gil09]; when M_K is proper, deĝ⟨Ẑ(y, t_1, ϕ_1), …, Ẑ(y, t_n, ϕ_n)⟩_{GS} = Σ_T deĝ_T(y, ϕ_K) over T with diagonal t_i, the nonsingular terms agreeing with (15.4.0.1) (at least in the hyperspecial case at inert primes).

items.name: Theorem 15.5.1 = Theorem 1.3.2 (arithmetic Siegel–Weil formula)
items.statement: In the situation of §14.2, assume F/F_0 is unramified at all finite places and split at all places above 2, and ϕ_K is inert-admissible and nonsingular at two places split in F. Then deĝ(z, ϕ_K) = c_K·∂Eis(z, ϕ_K); in particular deĝ(z, ϕ_K) is a nonholomorphic hermitian modular form of genus n. (Remark 15.5.2: the hypothesis forces F_0 ≠ Q, so Sh_K is projective and M_K proper, and V is nonsplit at some inert place, hence almost self-dual level (G2). Remark 15.5.3: such ϕ_K exist with Drinfeld levels at split places.)

routes.title: Siegel and PEL moduli problems, Part II: unitary Rapoport–Zink spaces, RSZ integral models and p-adic uniformization
routes.brief:
Start beyond Siegel and PEL moduli problems (PELModuli M0–M6), whose moduli functors with determinant condition (M1) and good-level representability and smoothness (M2) are imported. Construct the unitary objects that Li–Zhang, JAMS 35 (2022), 705–797, uses.

Import:
- Abelian schemes and arithmetic moduli (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A1–A4) for Serre–Tate and Grothendieck–Messing;
- finite flat groups and Dieudonné/Breuil–Kisin theory (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1, R07.2, R07.4, R07.6);
- Shimura data and complex Shimura varieties (ShimuraData D4–D5, ShimuraVarieties V1, V4–V6);
- the integral-model candidate Shimura varieties, Part II: integral models and reduction (ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII) only as a comparison, not as the construction.

The final theorems, stated exactly as the source does:
- N_n of signature (1, n − 1) over Spf O_F̆ (F/F_0 unramified, p > 2) is formally locally of finite type and formally smooth of relative dimension n − 1 (RZ96; Mihatsch Prop. 1.3), with the framing 𝔼, its canonical lifting, and 𝕍_n = Hom°(𝔼̄, 𝕏) the unique nonsplit hermitian space of dimension n.
- N^1_n at almost self-dual level is regular with semistable reduction (RSZ18 Thm. 5.1, Cho Thm. 1.2), and 𝕎_n is split.
- The auxiliary Ñ^1_n ⊆ N^1_n × N_{n+1} (lifts of α) has π_1 finite étale of degree q + 1 on generic fibres.
- The O_{F_0}-relative Dieudonné crystal, Grothendieck–Messing and Breuil modules hold for strict formal O_{F_0}-modules (Henniges, Faltings 2002).
- The Shimura datum G̃ = Z^Q ×_{G_m} G^Q has reflex field E_rE_Φ.
- The RSZ semi-global models: smooth at hyperspecial level (H1–H4, M1–M9; RSZ17b Thm. 4.1, RSZ19 Thm. 5.6(c)); flat and semistable at almost self-dual level (RSZ17b Thm. 4.7, Cho Prop. 1.4); smooth at split places, and regular with Drinfeld level under (D)(a)–(b); flat with isolated singularities at ramified places with the Krämer resolution (RSZ19 Thms. 5.4, 6.7, Def. 6.10).
- The model M_{K∩K^♯}.
- The global models M_{K°} under (G0)–(G4) and M_{K_m} under (G5).
- p-adic uniformization M̂^{ss} ≅ G̃′(Q)\[N′ × G̃(A^p_f)/K^p] with N = N, N^1 or Ñ^1 (RZ96; Cho Thm. 4.3; Mihatsch Thm. 4.1 at places ramified over p).

Keep the Eisenstein, sign, wedge and Lubin–Tate conditions explicit. Keep (D)(b), which the source adds to RSZ17b Thm. 4.5 to get regularity. Keep the signature conventions (1, n − 1) for Rapoport–Zink spaces and (n − 1, 1) for Shimura varieties distinct. Special cycles on these spaces belong to the consumer (UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles), so this Part II does not depend on it. Read RZ96 Chs. 3 and 6, RSZ17b §§3–4 and 8, RSZ18 §5, RSZ19 §§4–6 and Cho 2018 before closing. Tests: n = 1 (N_1 ≅ Spf O_F̆); the p-adic uniformization count at a point; and smooth versus merely flat models at an almost self-dual level.
routes.reason: PELModuli plans PEL moduli functors and representability only at good level, and ShimuraData D5's examples do not include this datum. Nothing in the atlas plans Rapoport–Zink spaces as formal moduli, parahoric or Drinfeld-level unitary models, or p-adic uniformization. These are new layers in PELModuli's direction.

routes.title: Gross–Zagier formulas and arithmetic heights, Part II: unitary Kudla–Rapoport cycles and the arithmetic Siegel–Weil formula
routes.reason: No atlas stage plans special cycles on higher-dimensional unitary Rapoport–Zink spaces or Shimura varieties, their arithmetic intersection numbers, Deligne–Lusztig strata, the local Kudla–Rapoport conjecture, or the arithmetic Siegel–Weil formula. GZ plans the curve case of the same programme (GZ.6 generating series and incoherent kernels, GZ.7 local identities between intersection multiplicities and derivatives of local densities), so these are new layers in GZ's direction. General lattice, harmonic-analysis and cohomology inputs go to their existing owners.
R07.1 owns p-divisible groups and their Tate modules. Tate's full-faithfulness theorem over O_K, Hom(G, H) ≅ Hom_Γ(T_pG, T_pH), belongs there; Lemma 4.4.1 uses it.

sourceIssues.printed: "We may further assume that L^♭ + ⟨x⟩ is integral and has a basis (e′_1, …, e′_n) such that val(e′_i) = a′_i. Let L′^♭ = ⟨e′_1, …, e′_{n−1}⟩. Then we have Int_{L^♭,V}(x) = Int_{L′^♭,V}(x′), and ∂Den_{L^♭,V}(x) = ∂Den_{L′^♭,V}(x′), where x′ = e′_n."
sourceIssues.correction: Replace the two claimed equalities by the equality of differences: with φ = Int_{L^♭,V} − ∂Den_{L^♭,V} and φ′ = Int_{L′^♭,V} − ∂Den_{L′^♭,V}, Theorem 6.1.3 cancels the horizontal parts, so φ(x) = Int(L^♭ + ⟨x⟩) − ∂Den(L^♭ + ⟨x⟩) = Int(L′^♭ + ⟨x′⟩) − ∂Den(L′^♭ + ⟨x′⟩) = φ′(x′). The induction hypothesis φ′ = 0 then gives φ(x) = 0 for x ∉ M(L^♭), which is all the rest of the proof uses.
sourceIssues.reason: Only the full functions Int_{L^♭}(x) = Int(L^♭ + ⟨x⟩) and ∂Den_{L^♭}(x) depend on the lattice L^♭ + ⟨x⟩ alone. Their horizontal and vertical parts depend on the hyperplane L^♭_F. By Definition 6.1.2, ∂Den_{L^♭,H}(x) and ∂Den_{L′^♭,H}(x′) are sums over integral L″ ⊇ L^♭ + ⟨x⟩ = L′^♭ + ⟨x′⟩ with the different conditions t(L″ ∩ L^♭_F) ≤ 1 and t(L″ ∩ L′^♭_F) ≤ 1; geometrically, Z(L^♭)_H ≠ Z(L′^♭)_H. So the two stated equalities do not follow from what precedes them. The step is repaired in one line and the theorem stands.
